topic: Discovery topic: why can silence feel uncomfortable? Aim: research psychological and behavioral science findings about why many people find silence -- especially unexpected silence in conversation, or being alone without any stimulation or activity -- uncomfortable or unpleasant. Cover findings such as: research on awkward or uncomfortable silences in conversation, research on people's general preference for having something to do rather than sitting alone with only their own thoughts (including studies where participants chose to self-administer a mild electric shock rather than sit quietly with their thoughts), physiological or arousal responses associated with silence or unstructured alone time, and any documented individual or cultural variation in how comfortable people are with silence. Use only facts confirmed by web search (no invented details, no facts supplied from the assistant's own prior knowledge).

kept_facts.claim: In Study 1, a brief silence inserted into an imagined group conversation was followed by higher reported rejection and negative emotion, and lower reported belonging, self-esteem, social validation, and perceived consensus than a fluent-conversation condition. ([pure.rug.nl](https://pure.rug.nl/ws/files/146971883/Disrupting_the_flow_How_brief_silences_in_group_conversations_affect.pdf))
kept_facts.subject: Brief silence disrupting conversational flow
kept_facts.scope: 102 undergraduate participants; 57 female; randomized to fluent-conversation or disrupted-flow conditions
kept_facts.conditions: Participants read a scenario in which a mildly controversial statement was followed either by continued conversation or by a brief silent moment.
kept_facts.source_title: Disrupting the flow: How brief silences in group conversations affect social needs
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: The study manipulated a brief silence in an imagined group-conversation scenario; do not generalize to every form of silence.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Study 1は102名（女性57名）をflow条件とdisrupted-flow条件に無作為割付し、想像上の会話で短い沈黙を操作している。沈黙条件では、拒絶感とネガティブ感情が高く、belonging、self-esteem、social validation、perceived consensusが低かった。因果表現も、無作為化された実験操作に基づく範囲では妥当。([rug.nl](https://www.rug.nl/staff/n.koudenburg/koudenburgetal.2011.pdf))

kept_facts.claim: In Study 2, a single four-second silence in a six-minute video conversation produced more reported rejection and negative emotion, less positive emotion, and lower belonging, self-esteem, social validation, and perceived consensus than the fluent-conversation condition; participants were generally unaware of the specific silence. ([pure.rug.nl](https://pure.rug.nl/ws/files/146971883/Disrupting_the_flow_How_brief_silences_in_group_conversations_affect.pdf))
kept_facts.subject: Unexpected four-second silence in conversation
kept_facts.scope: 60 undergraduate participants; randomized across fluent, disrupted-flow, and base-rate conditions
kept_facts.conditions: The silence followed a statement in a videotaped conversation; the source states that four seconds was selected to remain below conscious awareness while still disrupting perceived conversational flow.
kept_facts.source_title: Disrupting the flow: How brief silences in group conversations affect social needs
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Use precise wording such as 'a four-second silence in this experiment was sufficient to...' rather than claiming that four seconds is universally awkward.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Study 2は60名をflow、disrupted-flow、baserateの3条件に無作為割付し、6分間の動画中、発言後に4秒の沈黙を挿入した。disrupted-flow条件では拒絶感・ネガティブ感情が高く、ポジティブ感情、belonging、self-esteem、social validation、perceived consensusが低かった。4秒の沈黙は、参加者が通常は意識的に検出しにくい一方で会話の快適さを損なうよう、予備試験で選定されていた。『一般に気づかなかった』という表現も、編集に気づいた4名がいたため『大半は気づかなかった』という意味に限れば妥当。([rug.nl](https://www.rug.nl/staff/n.koudenburg/koudenburgetal.2011.pdf))

kept_facts.claim: In natural ten-minute conversations, long gaps between turns were more common among friends than among strangers; long gaps reduced momentary connection for strangers but increased momentary connection for friends. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9985966/?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.subject: Relationship context and long conversational gaps
kept_facts.scope: 261 stranger dyads and 65 friend dyads; 10-minute unstructured conversations
kept_facts.conditions: A long gap was defined as more than two seconds without verbal speech between turns.
kept_facts.numeric_value: 261 stranger dyads; 65 friend dyads; >2 seconds; 10 minutes
kept_facts.source_title: Long gaps between turns are awkward for strangers but not for friends
kept_facts.ambiguity: The study measured naturally occurring gaps rather than experimentally assigning gap lengths in the recorded conversations.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: The finding is context-dependent: long gaps did not have a uniformly negative meaning.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 研究本文・要旨は、2秒超のlong gapについて、友人 dyad の方が stranger dyad より多く、stranger では長いgapがconnection低下と関連し、friendではconnection上昇と関連したと報告している。261 stranger dyads、65 friend dyadsというscopeも独立検索で確認できる。なお、LedgerのDOI欄はこの論文のDOIではなく、論文自体はPMC掲載版と正しい書誌情報で確認できる。([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9985966/?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: Independent observers rated long gaps in stranger conversations as more awkward than equally long gaps in friend conversations, and perceived awkwardness increased more strongly with gap length for strangers. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9985966/?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.subject: Perceived awkwardness of long conversational gaps
kept_facts.scope: 100 video clips: 50 from stranger conversations and 50 from friend conversations
kept_facts.conditions: Clips represented five gap-length intervals: 2–2.5, 2.5–3, 3–3.5, 3.5–4, and more than 4 seconds.
kept_facts.numeric_value: 100 clips; 50 stranger; 50 friend; five duration intervals
kept_facts.source_title: Long gaps between turns are awkward for strangers but not for friends
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: The result concerns observers' ratings of video clips and should not be presented as a universal physiological response to silence.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Study 2では、stranger会話50本、friend会話50本の計100動画クリップを独立評定者が評価し、各関係条件に5つのgap長区間を設けている。awkwardnessはstrangerのlong gapで高く、gapが長くなるほどstrangerでの上昇が強かった。これは第三者による動画評定の結果であり、普遍的な生理反応を示すものではないというLedgerの限定も妥当。LedgerのDOI欄には書誌情報の誤りがあるが、主張自体は論文本文で確認できる。([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9985966/?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: Across 11 studies, participants generally did not enjoy spending 6–15 minutes alone with nothing to do but think, and they rated mundane external activities as more enjoyable than simply thinking. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1126/SCIENCE.1250830?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.subject: Preference for external activity over unstructured solitary thought
kept_facts.scope: Participants across 11 experimental studies; the paper's abstract does not provide one combined sample size
kept_facts.conditions: Participants were left alone for a short period with no external activity, or assigned to mundane activities in comparison conditions.
kept_facts.source_title: Just think: The challenges of the disengaged mind
kept_facts.ambiguity: The paper reports results across multiple studies with different samples and procedures; the finding is not a single-population estimate.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Avoid wording that implies everyone dislikes quiet thought; the source reports a general experimental tendency with substantial individual variation.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Wilson et al.の研究は、複数研究で6～15分、外部刺激のない部屋で思考する条件を用い、平均的には『just thinking』をあまり楽しまず、読書・音楽・ウェブ閲覧などの外的活動をより楽しむ傾向を報告している。個人差があるというLedgerの限定も適切。なお、LedgerのDOI欄は別論文を指しており、該当論文の書誌情報にはDOI誤記がある。([dtg.sites.fas.harvard.edu](https://dtg.sites.fas.harvard.edu/WILSON%20ET%20AL%202014.pdf))

kept_facts.claim: In the electric-shock study, 55 undergraduates spent 15 minutes alone with their thoughts while retaining the option to self-administer a previously experienced mild electric shock; the study reported that many participants chose the shock rather than remain without external stimulation. ([david-reinhard.com](https://www.david-reinhard.com/uploads/2/7/2/9/27296817/wilson_et_al_%282014%29_science_-_just_think.pdf?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.subject: Self-administered mild electric shock during solitary thought
kept_facts.scope: 55 undergraduate participants; 31 female and 24 male according to the study materials
kept_facts.conditions: Participants first evaluated the shock and then sat alone for 15 minutes with a button that could deliver the shock again.
kept_facts.source_title: Just think: The challenges of the disengaged mind
kept_facts.ambiguity: The commonly repeated gender percentages are based on a subset and should not be treated as percentages for all 55 participants without specifying the analysis sample.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: State that many participants self-administered the shock; do not imply that most participants preferred shock for the entire 15-minute period.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Study 10の参加者は55名の大学生（女性31名、男性24名）で、補足資料では15分間一人で思考し、ボタンで既経験の軽い電気ショックを自己投与できた。ショックを不快と評価した42名を主分析対象とし、そのうち男性12/18、女性6/24が少なくとも1回ショックを選択したため、『多くの参加者』という表現は妥当。ただし、ショック選択率は分析対象42名か全55名かで異なるため、全55名の割合と解釈しない必要がある。LedgerのDOI欄は別論文を指している。([dtg.sites.fas.harvard.edu](https://dtg.sites.fas.harvard.edu/WILSON%20ET%20AL%202014.pdf))

kept_facts.claim: In a replication conducted with 2,557 participants at 12 sites in 11 countries, participants assigned to do an everyday activity reported significantly greater enjoyment than participants assigned to think for pleasure in every country sampled. ([khu.elsevierpure.com](https://khu.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/cross-cultural-consistency-and-relativity-in-the-enjoyment-of-thi/))
kept_facts.subject: Cross-cultural preference for doing versus thinking for pleasure
kept_facts.scope: 2,557 participants; 12 sites; 11 countries; participants were college students
kept_facts.conditions: Participants were randomly assigned either to think for pleasure or to engage in an everyday solitary activity such as reading or watching a video.
kept_facts.source_title: Cross-Cultural Consistency and Relativity in the Enjoyment of Thinking Versus Doing
kept_facts.ambiguity: The countries and sites were a broad but non-global sample of college-student populations.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: The finding supports a cross-sample tendency, not a claim that all cultures or all individuals prefer activity over thought.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 2,557名、12 sites、11 countriesのreplicationで、各国とも、think for pleasure条件よりeveryday activity条件の参加者の方が有意に高いenjoymentを報告した。『every country sampled』は要旨の記述と一致する。ただし、サンプルは全世界の代表標本ではなく、Ledgerの限定も妥当。([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30035566/?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: The magnitude of the country differences in enjoyment of thinking for pleasure was statistically accounted for by variation in five individual-difference variables: need for cognition, openness to experience, meditation experience, initial positive affect, and reported phone usage, with phone usage negatively related to enjoyment. ([dtg.sites.fas.harvard.edu](https://dtg.sites.fas.harvard.edu/BUTTRICKETAL2019.pdf))
kept_facts.subject: Individual differences associated with enjoyment of solitary thought
kept_facts.scope: Cross-cultural college-student sample nested within the 2,557-participant, 11-country dataset
kept_facts.conditions: Associations were examined using multilevel and structural-equation models; the source describes these as predictors or correlates, not experimentally manipulated causes.
kept_facts.numeric_value: 5 individual-difference variables; 8 initially examined as significant correlates
kept_facts.source_title: Cross-Cultural Consistency and Relativity in the Enjoyment of Thinking Versus Doing
kept_facts.ambiguity: The statistical model accounted for country-level differences; it does not prove that these traits or behaviors caused enjoyment differences.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Use 'was associated with' or 'statistically accounted for variation in,' not 'caused.'
kept_facts.verification_notes: 要旨は、国ごとのthinking enjoymentの差が、need for cognition、openness、meditation experience、initial positive affectの正の関連と、reported phone usageの負の関連からなる5個の個人差変数によって完全に説明されたと報告している。Ledgerが相関・統計的説明であり因果ではないと限定している点も適切。([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30035566/?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: Across four studies, solitude generally reduced both high-arousal positive affect and high-arousal negative affect; solitude was associated with relaxation and reduced stress when participants actively chose to be alone. ([selfdeterminationtheory.org](https://selfdeterminationtheory.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/2018_NguyenRyanDeci_PSPB.pdf?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.subject: Affective arousal during solitude
kept_facts.scope: Four experimental studies reported in one research program
kept_facts.conditions: Conditions varied in whether participants were alone, engaged in an activity, chose what to think about, or actively chose to be alone.
kept_facts.source_title: Solitude as an Approach to Affective Self-Regulation
kept_facts.ambiguity: The result concerns affective self-report measures and solitude conditions, not complete sensory deprivation or every form of silence.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: This research provides evidence that unstructured alone time can reduce arousal for some conditions, contrasting with studies in which people prefer external activity.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 4研究を含む研究プログラムの要旨は、solitudeが高覚醒のポジティブ感情・ネガティブ感情を一般に低下させ、actively chosen solitudeではrelaxationとreduced stressにつながり得ると報告している。『solitude一般』をすべてのsilenceや感覚遮断へ拡張していないLedgerの限定も妥当。([journals.sagepub.com](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0146167217733073))

kept_facts.claim: In a study summarized by Pfeifer and Wittmann, students instructed to occupy themselves with their own thoughts during 6 minutes 30 seconds of silent solitary time reported greater relaxation, better mood, and lower arousal afterward than beforehand. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2020.00602/pdf?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.subject: Self-reported arousal and mood after silent solitary thought
kept_facts.scope: Student participants in a university seminar-room study; the review describes the silent interval but does not state the sample size in the cited passage
kept_facts.conditions: Participants sat alone, remained awake and seated, and were instructed to occupy themselves with their own thoughts; the duration was not disclosed in advance.
kept_facts.source_title: Waiting, Thinking, and Feeling: Variations in the Perception of Time During Silence
kept_facts.ambiguity: The result is based on self-report before–after comparisons in a student sample and does not establish that silence is relaxing for everyone.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Distinguish self-reported arousal from physiological arousal measured by autonomic sensors.
kept_facts.verification_notes: レビュー掲載の学生研究では、参加者は6分30秒、事前に長さを知らされず、座って自分の思考で過ごした。終了後は開始前よりrelaxed、better mood、less arousedと自己報告した。これは自己報告の前後比較であり、生理指標ではないというLedgerの注意書きも正しい。([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7142212/?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: In a within-participant study of 46 students, 6 minutes 30 seconds of silence increased relaxation in both a university seminar room and a city-garden setting; participants reported less boredom and greater present-moment orientation in the outdoor setting. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2020.00602/full))
kept_facts.subject: Environmental context, boredom, and relaxation during silence
kept_facts.scope: 46 students; 42 women and 4 men; age range 20–52; mean age 23.5
kept_facts.conditions: Each participant experienced silent periods indoors and outdoors, with one week between sessions; the duration was unknown to participants.
kept_facts.numeric_value: N=46; 6 minutes 30 seconds; 42 women; 4 men; age range 20–52
kept_facts.source_title: Waiting, Thinking, and Feeling: Variations in the Perception of Time During Silence
kept_facts.ambiguity: The sample consisted mainly of students from one German university, limiting generalizability.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: The setting altered the experience of silence; do not describe 'silence' as an isolated variable without the indoor/outdoor condition.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Study 5は46名（女性42名、男性4名、平均年齢23.5歳、範囲20～52歳）を対象に、屋内と市街地の庭園で各6分30秒の沈黙を体験させたwithin-participant研究である。両環境でrelaxationが増え、屋外ではboredomが少なく、現在志向が高かったという記述と一致する。主に一大学の学生標本という一般化上の限定も妥当。([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7142212/?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: A systematic review of 37 studies concluded that autonomic responses to silence differ according to whether silence is conceptualized as inner silence or outer silence, and may also depend on context, familiarity with silence, surrounding noise, and empathy. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37714570/?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.subject: Autonomic nervous-system responses associated with silence
kept_facts.scope: 37 studies included after searches of PubMed, Scopus, PsycINFO, EMBASE, and Google Scholar through July 2023
kept_facts.conditions: The review distinguished internally cultivated or experienced silence from externally quiet conditions.
kept_facts.numeric_value: 37 included studies; literature searched through July 2023
kept_facts.source_title: Silence and its effects on the autonomic nervous system: A systematic review
kept_facts.ambiguity: The review uses a theoretical distinction between inner and outer silence and synthesizes heterogeneous studies; it does not establish one universal autonomic response.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Do not claim that silence always lowers physiological arousal; the review explicitly describes context-dependent responses.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 2023年のsystematic reviewは511件を検索し37研究を採用した。要旨は、inner silenceとouter silenceで自律神経反応が異なり、context、silenceへのfamiliarity、周囲のnoise、empathyなどにも左右されると明記している。単一の普遍的反応を主張していない点も適切。([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37714570/))

kept_facts.claim: In a counterbalanced EKG experiment, participants experienced eight-minute periods of silence, fMRI acoustic noise, and white noise; parasympathetic activity was higher during fMRI noise than during silence, while sympathetic activity was higher during white noise than during fMRI noise. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8615429/?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.subject: Autonomic activity during silence versus auditory noise
kept_facts.scope: Healthy human participants without specified neuropsychiatric, hearing, medication, or relevant medical conditions in the cited source passage
kept_facts.conditions: Each condition lasted eight minutes; condition order was counterbalanced; autonomic measures were derived from EKG R–R intervals.
kept_facts.source_title: fMRI Acoustic Noise Enhances Parasympathetic Activity in Humans
kept_facts.ambiguity: The study compared laboratory silence with specific high-intensity auditory stimuli; it does not establish how unexpected conversational silence affects autonomic activity.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: This result is a counterexample to the assumption that silence is automatically the most physiologically calming auditory condition.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 30名の健康な参加者が、counterbalancedな8分間のsilence、fMRI acoustic noise、white noise条件を経験した。EKG由来指標では、parasympathetic activityはfMRI noiseでsilenceより高く、sympathetic activityはwhite noiseでfMRI noiseより高かった。原論文は神経精神疾患、聴覚障害、中枢神経作用薬、関連する医学的状態を除外基準として明記しているため、Ledgerのscopeは『条件が不明』ではなく『それらの条件を持たない健康参加者』と読むのが正確。([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8615429/))

kept_facts.claim: In a Japan–United States survey study, Japanese respondents reported a more negative view of silence with strangers than with close friends, whereas Americans did not show that relationship; Americans reported more strategic use of silence than Japanese respondents. ([journals.sagepub.com](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0022022198295005))
kept_facts.subject: Cultural and relational variation in attitudes toward conversational silence
kept_facts.scope: Respondents from Japan and the United States; the accessible source excerpt does not state the full sample size
kept_facts.conditions: Attitudes were examined separately for communication with strangers and close friends.
kept_facts.source_title: Silence in Japan and the United States
kept_facts.ambiguity: The accessible abstract does not provide the sample size or detailed sampling frame; findings concern reported attitudes rather than observed conversational behavior.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Avoid broad cultural stereotypes; the source itself reports that relationship context changes the pattern.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 1998年の日本・米国比較研究の要旨は、日本人ではstrangersとの会話でclose friendsよりsilenceを否定的に見る傾向があったが、米国人ではその関係が見られず、米国人の方がstrategic use of silenceを多く報告したと記載している。relationship contextを含む限定も正しい。([journals.sagepub.com](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0022022198295005?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: In a staged one-to-one tutorial study, Japanese and UK undergraduates showed similar tolerance of instructor silence and similar discomfort: the groups differed by only about seven seconds in mean silence tolerance, and both groups' average discomfort was around 4 on a 1–6 scale; silence duration was not correlated with discomfort. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12564-017-9503-8))
kept_facts.subject: Cross-cultural comparison of tolerance for silence
kept_facts.scope: Initial sample: 20 Japanese and 15 UK first-year undergraduates; quantitative analysis retained 34 participants after exclusions
kept_facts.conditions: An instructor adopted a neutral, silent posture during a staged one-to-one tutorial; students could end the silence by speaking.
kept_facts.numeric_value: Japan n=20; UK n=15; quantitative analysis n=34; approximately 7-second mean difference; discomfort approximately 4/6
kept_facts.numeric_scope: Participant groups and reported group comparisons
kept_facts.source_title: Talk, silence and anxiety during one-to-one tutorials: A cross-cultural comparative study of Japan and UK undergraduates’ tolerance of silence
kept_facts.ambiguity: The study used small, intact classes and a specific instructor–student context; it should not be treated as a representative national comparison.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: This study found similarities rather than a simple Japan-versus-UK difference, showing that context and individual reactions matter.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 日本20名、英国15名のfirst-year undergraduatesを対象にし、UK参加者1名を外れ値、別のUK参加者1名を携帯電話の着信で除外したため、量的分析は34名となった。日本群の平均沈黙耐久時間は英国群より7秒強長かったが有意差はなく、平均不快感は英国4.29、日本4.85（6段階）で、本文の『両群とも約4』という要約は許容範囲。沈黙時間と不快感の相関も有意ではなかった。([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007%2Fs12564-017-9503-8.pdf))

note: CONFIRMED(VERIFIED)のみ採用。AMBIGUOUS/REJECTEDはfact_ledger_verification.jsonに記録済みだが本Ledgerからは除外した。
